land.text: the Boeotian cities, which Thebes kept when the hegemony ended

predecessors.note: The same Theban state after the hegemony: Cliopatria splits it at -351/-350 ('Sacred Band of Thebes' then 'Thebans'); the pages date the end of the hegemony to 362, so the hand-over is moved to -361.

land.text: Philip 'did not, however, dissolve the Boeotian Confederacy'; Thebes surrendered and received a Macedonian garrison

successors.note: After Chaeronea (August 338) Boeotia is a Macedonian-controlled member of the Greek states (League of Corinth, 'formed in the latter half of 337 BC'); Cliopatria's greek-city-states row regains Boeotia in -337. Thebes was destroyed by Alexander in 335 (Thebes page).

capitals.name: Thebes (Thiva)
capitals.note: The Boeotian League page puts the federal council 'at Thebes' (for 395 BC) and says Thebes 'made it a suitable capital'; no later date. At Chaeronea 'Philip marched first to Thebes, which surrendered to him' (Chaeronea page).

correction.text: the Boeotian cities, with the allied lands gone after Mantinea

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria keeps the 33,821 km2 hegemony shape ('Sacred Band of Thebes') to -351, but the Theban hegemony page says the hegemony 'ended with the tactical Theban victory at Mantinea in 362 BC' and the Epaminondas page that 'the Thebans returned to their more traditional defensive policy'. What is left is Boeotia (14 cells, about 3,500 km2); no page opened gives an area. The Third Sacred War page lists Thessaly, Locris and Doris as allies of Thebes against Phocis (356-346), not as Theban land.

correction.text: Boeotia: 'Philip restored to Boeotia the cities that Phocis had captured during the war'. Holds -350..-338 except -347..-346, when Orchomenus and Coronea are held by Phocis (ledger loss and gain)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 5,164 km2 (18 cells) against the Boeotia region's 14 cells (about 3,500 km2): the shape reaches Lamia and Thermopylae (Locris, Malis) and misses five Boeotian cells. The Third Sacred War infobox puts Locris and Doris with Thebes as allies, and Philip garrisoned Nicaea, 'the closest town to Thermopylae,' with Thessalian troops, so the northern cells are not Theban. The page gives no area; the Boeotian League infobox is garbled and the Thebes infobox gives only the modern municipality (830 km2).

region.text: the Boeotian cities, the league Thebes led

ledger.note: 361: after Mantinea Thebes falls back on the Boeotian League. The Theban hegemony page: 'It ended with the tactical Theban victory at Mantinea in 362 BC.' The Epaminondas page: 'With Epaminondas removed from the scene, the Thebans returned to their more traditional defensive policy'. This is the same Theban state as the previous dossier, split here at the end of the hegemony instead of at Cliopatria's -351/-350. The year 361 is the first year after the hegemony; the pages give no event for it.

region.text: Delphi and the Phocis-Boeotia frontier around Chaeronea and Orchomenus

ledger.note: 356: Phocis seizes Delphi and the Third Sacred War begins. 'In approximately July 356 BC, Philomelus marched on Delphi' and 'easily captured the city of Delphi'; the fine of 357 was imposed 'by the Amphictyonic League', which Thebes dominated. Thebes's own first dated campaigns are Neon (355 in Buckler, 354 in other historians) and, in 353, Onomarchos's invasion of Doris and 'eventually Boeotia', stopped 'close to Chaeronea'. The zone is Delphi and the Phocian side of the Boeotian frontier; Phocis has no dossier.

region.text: The Phocians had occupied several Boeotian cities (Orchomenos, Coroneia and Corsiae)

ledger.note: 347: Phocian garrisons hold the Boeotian cities of Orchomenus, Coronea and Corsiae. 'The Phocians had occupied several Boeotian cities, but were running out of treasure to pay their mercenaries'; after Phalaikos's fall 'three new generals' 'successfully attacked Boeotia again' and 'the Thebans were unable to act effectively against the Phocians' by 347-346. The page does not say when the cities were taken (page silent); Onomarchos had invaded Boeotia in 353 and was 'finally controlled by the allied Boeotians close to Chaeronea'. 347 is a bridge date.

region.text: Philip restored to Boeotia the cities that Phocis had captured during the war

ledger.note: 346: Philip gives the captured Boeotian cities back to Thebes. 'Philip restored to Boeotia the cities that Phocis had captured during the war' (Orchomenos, Coroneia, Corsiae). The sentence carries no year; it belongs to the page's settlement of 346, after Phalaikos surrendered Phocis on 19 July. The page is silent on any other gain for Thebes.

346: Phocis surrenders and the Third Sacred War ends. Phalaikos surrendered Phocis on 19 July in return for being allowed to leave with his mercenaries (the page's account); result 'Amphictyonic League victory'; the Phocian cities were to be destroyed but 'they retained their land'. The Thebes page, by contrast, says 'In the Third Sacred War (356-346 BC) with its neighbor Phocis, Thebes lost its predominance in central Greece.'

region.text: Philip marched first to Thebes, which surrendered to him

ledger.note: 338: Philip wins at Chaeronea and Thebes surrenders. 'in August 338 BC, Philip's army marched straight down the main road from Phocis to Boeotia'; 'Philip marched first to Thebes, which surrendered to him; he expelled the Theban leaders who had opposed him' and 'installed a Macedonian garrison'; he 'did not, however, dissolve the Boeotian Confederacy' and ordered Plataea and Thespiae re-founded. Result: 'Macedon establishes hegemony over the majority of Greece (except Sparta)'. The month is the battle's; the surrender is undated. Thebes revolted and was destroyed in 335 (Thebes page).

wars.name: Third Sacred War
wars.outcome: Amphictyonic League victory: Phocis was expelled from the Amphictyonic council and its cities ordered destroyed, but it kept its land; Philip restored the Boeotian cities Phocis had captured and Macedon took Phocis's two votes.
wars.note: Infobox sides: Amphictyonic League, Thebes, Boeotian League, Thessaly, Locris, Doris, Macedon against Phocis, Pherae, Athens, Sparta. Philip won at the Crocus Field in 352; Thermopylae was his by 9 July 346.

wars.name: Battle of Chaeronea (338 BC)
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory; Thebes surrendered and took a Macedonian garrison, the Second Athenian League was dissolved and the League of Corinth followed in the latter half of 337.

certainty.note: The Boeotian frontier is not given by any page opened; the Phocian frontier is approximate and Philip's settlement of 346 restored cities, not a surveyed line.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Thebans' (-350..-338, 5,164 km2) is the Boeotia-only Theban state after the hegemony. It is the same state as 'Sacred Band of Thebes' (-366..-351); the two rows are kept as two dossiers because the brief lists them separately, and the split is moved from Cliopatria's -351/-350 to the real hinge, Mantinea (362), so this dossier starts at -361 with a new keyframe for -361..-351 (the Cliopatria hegemony shape is not used after -362). The colour agent may give both the same hue family; a reviewer who prefers one state can merge the two under the earlier slug with both Names. Cliopatria's Wikipedia title for the row is 'Theban', which was not opened (it names a people, not the state); the Thebes, Boeotian League, Third Sacred War and Chaeronea pages were used instead. Page budget (1-2) exceeded: the Boeotian pages are silent on area and borders, so every extent is the Boeotia region with trims; the Phocian occupation (loss 347) is a bridge date, the page being silent. Disagreement: the Third Sacred War page ends in an 'Amphictyonic League victory' with Thebes on the winning side, while the Thebes page says Thebes 'lost its predominance in central Greece' in that war. Neighbour mirrors: greek-city-states /ledger/42 gains Boeotia from this state in -337 (this dossier ends in August 338; the year differs by one); Phocis, the occupier of 347-346, has no dossier and is listed for the orchestrator; macedonian-empire has no event for the garrison at Thebes. Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer lacks: Orchomenus, Coronea, Chaeronea (places).
